rejected.title: Validity
card: An investigation is valid when it tests what it set out to test. The method must measure the thing the question asks about.
The independent variable is the one you change. The dependent variable is the one you measure.
Controlled variables are all the other factors you keep the same. If one of them changes too, you cannot tell what caused the result.
A fair method changes only the independent variable and measures only the dependent variable. This makes the conclusion trustworthy.
rejected.remember: A valid test changes one thing, measures the right thing and keeps everything else the same.

a.q: Why must controlled variables be kept the same in an investigation?
opts: So only the independent variable can explain the result
So the dependent variable stays the same in every trial
So the independent variable changes by the same amount
So the results come out as the student predicted
a.why: If the other factors stay the same, any change in the dependent variable can be linked to the independent variable. The dependent variable is meant to change, so keeping it constant would defeat the test.
a.clue: Think about what you could blame if two things changed.

b.q: Priya tests whether fertiliser affects bean plant height. She gives Plant A fertiliser in a sunny window and Plant B none in a dark cupboard. Why is her test not valid?
opts: Light also differs, so two things could explain the result
Height does not show plant growth, so she measured wrongly
Fertiliser is a controlled variable, so it must stay fixed
Using two plants is wrong, as a fair test uses one plant
b.why: Fertiliser and light both differ, so either could explain the height difference. Her question is about height, so measuring height is the right dependent variable and is not the problem.
b.clue: Count how many things differ between the two plants.

version.title: Validity
card: An investigation is valid when it tests what it set out to test. The method must measure the thing the question asks about.
The independent variable is the one you change. The dependent variable is the one you measure.
Controlled variables are all the other factors you keep the same. If one of them changes too, you cannot tell what caused the result.

A fair method changes only the independent variable and measures its effect on the dependent variable. Scientists may also check controlled variables, such as temperature, to make sure they stay the same.
version.remember: A valid test changes one thing, measures its effect and keeps everything else the same.

opts: So only the independent variable can explain the result

a.clue: Think about what you could blame if two things changed.

b.q: Kai tests whether salt water affects how tall bean plants grow. Plant A gets salt water on a sunny windowsill, and Plant B gets tap water in a dark cupboard. Why is his test not valid?
opts: Light also differs, so two things could explain the result
Height does not show plant growth, so he measured wrongly
Salt is a controlled variable, so it should stay the same
A fair test uses one plant, so using two plants is wrong
b.why: Salt and light both differ between the plants, so either could explain a difference in height. His question is about height, so measuring height is the right dependent variable and is not the problem.
b.clue: Count how many things differ between the two plants.
